api:
<Forest data={trials} name={|s: &Study| s.name} estimate={|s: &Study| s.effect}
    low={|s: &Study| s.low} high={|s: &Study| s.high} weight={|s: &Study| s.patients} null={1.} />
PropTypeDefault
estimateFn(&T) -> f64: the point estimaterequired
low, highFn(&T) -> f64: the confidence intervalrequired
weightFn(&T) -> f64: sizes each square, such as the study sizeequal squares
nullf64: the dashed line of no effect0.
colorcolourthe first series colour
value_axisAxisConfig; pass .scale(ScaleKind::Log { base: 10. }) for ratiosAxisConfig::new()
tooltip, classas on <XYChart>

One row per study, in your order from the top. Each row is a line from low to high with a square at estimate. Built on <XYChart>, so the squares can be hovered.

examples.title: Hazard ratios
examples.description: One row per trial on a log axis; square size follows trial size, and the dashed line marks no effect.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn ratios() {
    let data = use_signal(trials());
    rsx! { <Forest data={data} name={|s: &Study| s.name} estimate={|s: &Study| s.effect} low={|s: &Study| s.low} high={|s: &Study| s.high} weight={|s: &Study| s.patients} null={1.} value_axis={AxisConfig::new().scale(ScaleKind::Log { base: 10. }).label("Hazard ratio")} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Mean differences
examples.description: Equal-sized markers around a null of 0.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn differences() {
    let data = use_signal(
        trials()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|study| Study {
                effect: (study.effect - 1.) * 10.,
                low: (study.low - 1.) * 10.,
                high: (study.high - 1.) * 10.,
                ..study
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <Forest data={data} name={|s: &Study| s.name} estimate={|s: &Study| s.effect} low={|s: &Study| s.low} high={|s: &Study| s.high} value_axis={AxisConfig::new().label("Change in mmHg")} color={rgb(0x8839ef)} class="h-80" /> }
}
